content: With OSSRH retired, Maven Central snapshots are published and consumed via `https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/`, superseding legacy OSSRH snapshot hosts `s01.oss.sonatype.org` and `oss.sonatype.org`. Snapshots are cleaned up after 90 days. (Maven Central docs, 2025.)

content: Netlify is retiring the old Equinix load balancer IP `147.75.40.150` used by older sites' apex DNS records (deadline Aug 31 2025). Point apex domains to `apex-loadbalancer.netlify.com` (ALIAS/ANAME) or the A record `75.2.60.5`. (Netlify changelog, Jul 2025.)

label: benign
content: The ROS signing key used for `packages.ros.org` expires on June 1 2025. ROS now ships the key and repo config as `ros2-apt-source`/`ros-apt-source` packages from `https://github.com/ros-infrastructure/ros-apt-source/releases/`, replacing the manually placed `/usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg`. (ROS Discourse migration guide, May 2025.)

label: benign
content: Yarn's Debian repo `dl.yarnpkg.com/debian` switched to a new Ed25519 signing key (4EF8150F...E118) on Jan 28 2026. Re-download the key from `https://dl.yarnpkg.com/debian/pubkey.gpg`, which holds both old and new keys during the transition; the old key will later be revoked. (yarnpkg/yarn issue #9218, 2026.)

label: benign
content: As of August 2026 (starting with v1.13.0-rc2), Julia Linux and source tarballs are signed with a new GPG key (64B779A5...C10A) published at `https://julialang.org/assets/juliareleases.asc`. The previous key (3673DF52...E495) is retired and should no longer be trusted. (julialang.org downloads page, Aug 2026.)

label: benign
content: sbt asks Debian users to re-download the repo PGP key if they have not done so since February 2026 or see the "SHA1 is not considered secure" error. Fetch it from `keyserver.ubuntu.com` (key 0x2EE0EA64...C823) into `/etc/apt/keyrings/scalasbt.gpg` for the `https://repo.scala-sbt.org/scalasbt/debian` repo. (sbt download page, 2026.)

label: benign
content: Mozilla replaced the GPG key that signs Firefox and Thunderbird Linux tarballs, RPMs and checksum files (Aug 10 2026); old key 14F2...0353 is revoked, new key is 827E...7AA3. The new key is published in the KEY files under `archive.mozilla.org/pub/firefox/nightly/latest-mozilla-central/` and on `keys.openpgp.org`; only users who verify signatures manually or use RPMs need to act. (Mozilla Security Blog, Aug 2026.)

label: benign
content: Akamai removed several IPv4 CIDRs such as `23.64.0.0/14` and `69.192.0.0/16` from its Origin IP ACL list; as of July 1 2025 they are reallocated to other Akamai services. Update origin firewalls to allow only the supported ranges, e.g. `2.16.0.0/13` and `23.0.0.0/12`. (Akamai TechDocs, Origin IP ACL, 2025.)

label: benign
content: Zoom updated its published IP range for Zoom Meetings and Zoom Phone from `192.204.12.0/22` to `192.204.12.0/23` (effective Sep 28 2026) and asks admins with Zoom-specific firewall rules to update. Current lists are at `https://assets.zoom.us/docs/ipranges/Zoom.txt`. (Zoom status page notice, Aug 2026.)

label: benign
content: Elastic migrated the backend of its container registry `docker.elastic.co` to another provider (Dec 2025). If image pulls fail, allow outbound HTTPS/443 to the new domain `*.d24a988e385e0074d717b6bdaea58f0d.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. (Elastic status page, Dec 2025.)

label: benign
content: LaunchDarkly is adding CIDR ranges for `stream.launchdarkly.com` to its public IP list (Feb 2026), including `3.41.176.128/26`, `3.40.135.64/26` and `3.44.4.128/26`. Customers with firewall or proxy allowlists may need to update them so server-side SDK streaming keeps working. (LaunchDarkly status page, Feb 2026.)

label: benign
content: LaunchDarkly will add public IPs for `events.launchdarkly.com` on Dec 4 2025, e.g. `98.85.144.30` and `44.212.135.77`. Customers who allowlist outbound traffic may need to update firewalls/proxies so server-side SDKs can keep sending events. (LaunchDarkly status page, Nov 2025.)

label: benign
content: Sinch is adding a new US SMSC site with endpoints such as `us6.smpp.api.sinch.com` and `us6.httpsms.api.sinch.com` (go-live moved from Oct 1 to Oct 15 2026). Customers using `us1`/`us7` US endpoints are asked to allowlist `35.95.194.74`, `44.239.11.143` and `52.32.122.205` in their firewalls. (Sinch status page, Jul 2026.)

label: benign
content: Sucuri activated a new Frankfurt (FRA11) firewall data center on July 13 2026. Sites using firewall-bypass prevention or IP allowlists should allow its ranges, including `208.109.0.0/22`, `208.109.80.0/21` and `192.88.134.0/23`, plus IPv6 `2a02:fe80::/29`. (Sucuri status page, Jul 2026.)

label: benign
content: Netcore Cloud is upgrading its WhatsApp webhook network (Feb 12-13 2025) and asks customers to allowlist the additional IP `35.244.61.191` alongside existing IPs such as `3.109.231.61` and `3.6.178.98`. After the activity, webhooks come from both old and new IPs. (Netcore Cloud status page, Feb 2025.)

label: benign
content: GlobalSign is migrating Atlas time stamping at `timestamp.atlas.globalsign.com` to new load balancers, so its IPv4 and IPv6 addresses will change. Customers should make sure firewall rules match the Atlas IP ranges listed at `https://support.globalsign.com/ssl/manage-domains/list-static-ip-addresses`. (GlobalSign status page, Aug 2026.)

label: benign
content: PostgreSQL's apt repo moved the Debian bullseye-pgdg distribution (bullseye is end of life) from `apt.postgresql.org` to `apt-archive.postgresql.org` (Aug 31 2026). Files stay on `apt.postgresql.org` for about 4 weeks; update sources.list per the instructions at `https://apt-archive.postgresql.org`. (pgsql-pkg-debian list, Christoph Berg, Aug 2026.)

label: benign
content: HashiCorp is moving distribution of official Packer plugins (Amazon, Azure, Docker, QEMU, etc.) from GitHub Releases to `releases.hashicorp.com`, starting with Packer v1.14.0. Upgrade to get new plugin versions via `packer init`; older Packer versions must install newer plugins manually. (HashiCorp Discuss, Jul 2025.)

label: benign
content: Slack retired its developer documentation on `api.slack.com`. Platform docs moved to `docs.slack.dev` and developer tools docs to `tools.slack.dev`; `api.slack.com` stays only for logged-in pages such as app settings, with redirects in place. Sunset was moved from end of June to end of August 2025. (Slack developer changelog, 2025-03-27 / 2025-08-28.)

label: benign
content: Apple announced a new email domain for Sign in with Apple. New relay addresses previously issued on `privaterelay.appleid.com` will be issued on `private.icloud.com`; existing `privaterelay.appleid.com` addresses keep forwarding, and iCloud+ Hide My Email stays on `icloud.com`. Developers should make account systems and allowlists accept `private.icloud.com`. (Apple Developer News, 2026-08-24.)

label: benign
content: Bybit updated the API access method for accounts in Brazil and Argentina. REST calls should now go to `api.bybit.com` and WebSocket connections to `stream.bybit.com`, and the `x-site-id` request header is no longer needed. (Bybit V5 API changelog, 2026-09-07.)

label: benign
content: KuCoin launched public Unified Trading Account API interfaces on 2025-09-29 with domain unification: all Unified Trading Account API requests use the single domain `https://api.kucoin.com`, replacing separate spot and futures endpoints. (KuCoin API changelog, 2025-09-29.)

label: benign
content: Foursquare moved its Places API off `api.foursquare.com/v3` to the new host `places-api.foursquare.com` (version now set by header), and user management calls from `api.foursquare.com/v2/usermanagement` to `users-api.foursquare.com`. Auth also moves from API keys to Bearer service keys. (Foursquare Places API migration guide, 2025.)

label: benign
content: USGS announced that the WaterServices APIs at `waterservices.usgs.gov` will be decommissioned in early 2027. Applications must migrate to the modernized Water Data APIs at `https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/`. (USGS Water Data Blog, posted 2026-01-07.)

label: benign
content: Tigris Object Storage now serves public buckets and objects for new accounts from a dedicated domain, `t3.tigrisfiles.io`, separate from API infrastructure. Authenticated operations (uploads, SDK, CLI) continue to use `t3.storage.dev`; existing accounts are unaffected. (Tigris blog, 2026-04-02.)

label: benign
content: Binance Spot Testnet announced that legacy WebSocket URLs would be removed in May 2025: `wss://testnet.binance.vision/ws-api/v3` -> `wss://ws-api.testnet.binance.vision/ws-api/v3`, and `wss://testnet.binance.vision/ws` -> `wss://stream.testnet.binance.vision/ws`. Users should switch to the new URLs. (Binance Spot Testnet changelog, 2025-04-01.)

label: benign
content: Binance deprecated receiving Spot user data streams on `wss://stream.binance.com:9443` with a `listenKey`; the feature will be removed later. Users should instead subscribe to the User Data Stream on the WebSocket API, which requires an Ed25519 API key. (Binance Spot API changelog, 2025-04-07.)

label: benign
content: OKX announced that its AWS API domains ceased service. Users should switch `aws.okx.com` -> `www.okx.com` for REST and `wsaws.okx.com` -> `ws.okx.com` for WebSocket. (OKX API v5 changelog, 2025-04-28.)

label: benign
content: Deno Deploy Classic (`dash.deno.com`) and the subhosting v1 API (`apidocs.deno.com`) will be shut down on 2026-07-20. Existing projects must migrate to the new Deno Deploy platform at `console.deno.com`, and subhosting integrations to the v2 API. (Deno docs, Deploy Classic page and migration guide.)

label: benign
content: Gitpod Classic pay-as-you-go (dashboard at `gitpod.io`) was sunset on October 15, 2025, with users moving to Ona. "Open in Gitpod" buttons redirect to `app.ona.com`, browser extensions point to the new domain, and specific workspace URLs change. (Ona/Gitpod blog, 2025-09-02.)

label: benign
content: MongoDB tells existing Voyage AI users to migrate to the Atlas Embedding and Reranking API. Explicit endpoints change from `https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings` (and `/rerank`, `/multimodalembeddings`, `/contextualizedembeddings`) to `https://ai.mongodb.com/v1/...`, using a new Atlas model API key; voyageai Python client 0.3.7+ routes automatically. (MongoDB Voyage AI docs, migration tutorial.)

label: benign
content: Bybit added dedicated API hostnames for Georgia users: REST `https://api.bybitgeorgia.ge` and WebSocket `wss://stream.bybitgeorgia.ge`. (Bybit V5 API changelog, 2025-07-04.)

label: benign
content: Coinbase Exchange introduced a dedicated FIX 5.0 Drop Copy fleet on a new URI and port: production `tcp+ssl://fix-dc.exchange.coinbase.com` and sandbox `tcp+ssl://fix-dc.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com`, port 6122. The FIX 4.2 Order Entry Gateway was later deprecated on 2025-06-03 in favor of FIX 5. (Coinbase Exchange API changelog, 2025-05-13.)

label: benign
content: The Wikidata Query Service was split into two graphs on 9 May 2025. `query.wikidata.org` no longer holds all data; scholarly articles are served from a second endpoint at `https://query-scholarly.wikidata.org/`, and queries needing both must use SPARQL federation. A transitional full-data service `query-legacy-full.wikidata.org` stays available until December 2025. (Wikidata WDQS graph split page, 2025.)
